paper.title_en: Projections and topological classification of black hole thermodynamics
paper.abstract_en: Black hole thermodynamic topology has evolved from classifications based on global topological numbers to more refined schemes including boundary behavior. This development motivates a deeper question: how are different topological manifestations connected within the complete thermodynamic structure? In this paper, we propose the thermodynamic projection conjecture, which seeks to address this question by examining different topological manifestations in the context of the complete thermodynamic structure and exploring their underlying physical connections and formation mechanisms. As a representative application of this idea, we investigate temperature-dependent thermodynamic topological phase transitions, in which the topological number varies with temperature while the physical parameters are held fixed. We examine how the complete thermodynamic structure gives rise to different topological outcomes on different temperature slices. Our results demonstrate that temperature-dependent thermodynamic topological phase transitions arise from boundary effects, whereas the pairwise generation or annihilation of equilibrium states in the interior leaves the total topological number unchanged. These results establish that, at fixed physical parameters, the topological differences observed on different temperature slices originate from the same complete thermodynamic structure and can be understood within a unified framework of thermodynamic projections. Furthermore, this study offers a new approach to understanding black hole thermodynamic structures and their rich physical behavior through the interplay between global structures and their local manifestations.
